findings.label: Suppurative granulomatous inflammation on histology
findings.evidence: dermal inflammatory infiltrate surrounding the lesion; suppurative granulomatous inflammation with bacterial granules

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E histopathology panel from a patient with botryomycosis showing dermal suppurative granulomatous inflammation and bacterial granules, consistent with the caption and in-text evidence. B: Higher-magnification H&E histopathology panel showing coccoid bacterial clusters and Splendore-Hoeppli material within a dermal abscess, diagnostic of botryomycosis.
panels.attribution_text: Limón Limón et al. Botryomycosis: A Case Series and Literature Review in Mexico.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.107815. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination showing suppurative granulomatous inflammation with bacterial granules. (A) Low-power view demonstrating dermal inflammatory infiltrate surrounding the lesion (H&E, 10×). (B) Higher magnification highlighting clusters of coccoid bacteria (black arrow) surrounded by eosinophilic material consistent with the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon (H&E, 40×)
in_text_mentions: At higher magnification, neutrophilic microabscesses containing amphophilic granules measuring 200-500 μm in diameter were identified. These granules consisted of clusters of coccoid bacteria surrounded by an eosinophilic material forming the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon, findings consistent with botryomycosis (Figures 3A, 3B).

panels.rationale: H&E histology of renal botryomycosis showing bacterial colonies surrounded by Splendore-Hoeppli material and inflammatory cells; caption and in-text support disease attribution.
panels.attribution_text: Mathew et al. Incidental renal botryomycosis in a nonfunctioning kidney.. Case reports in nephrology 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/239093. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Splendore Hoeppeli phenomenon surrounding bacterial colonies with inflammatory cells (H&E, ×20) Inset, Splendore Hoeppeli phenomenon (arrow head) (H&E, ×40).
in_text_mentions: ed periglomerular fibrosis. The renal parenchyma showed abscesses containing Gram negative organisms surrounded by amorphous eosinophilic material suggestive of Splendore Hoeppeli phenomenon (Figures 3 and 4). These bacterial colonies were negative for Grocott-Gomori silver and Ziehl-Neelson stains. A final diagnosis of renal botryomycosis superimposed on chronic pyelonephritis was rendered. The patient was treated with cefuroxime (2nd generation cephalosporin) for two weeks and prulifloxacin (new generation fluroquinolone) for 3 days. On followup, two years hence, the patient is asymptomatic

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of Case 2, a patient with oral botryomycosis at a dental extraction site, supported by the article's case series on botryomycosis. B: Clinical photograph of Case 3, a 17-year-old woman with a chronic ulcerated, purulent plaque on the thigh, consistent with cutaneous botryomycosis as described in the case series.
panels.attribution_text: Limón Limón et al. Botryomycosis: A Case Series and Literature Review in Mexico.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.107815. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
in_text_mentions: The patient reported a history of extraction of the right maxillary second molar. Three weeks after the procedure, exuberant granulation tissue developed at the surgical site, requiring local excision. However, the lesion recurred one month later, prompting surgical removal of the tumor (Figure 2A).

A 17-year-old woman with no relevant past medical history presented with a two-year history of a lesion located on the posterior aspect of the left thigh. Physical examination revealed an ovoid plaque measuring 12 × 7 × 4 cm, erythematous and hyperpigmented, with a centrally ulcerated area draining purulent exudate. The surface was covered with serohemorrhagic crusts, and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation was observed in the surrounding skin. The lesion had poorly defined borders and was infiltrated on palpation (Figure 2B).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of a large exophytic ulcerated tumor on the right great toe in a case titled exophytic botryomycosis; the unusual exophytic presentation supports atypical typicality. B: Closer view of the same exophytic ulcerated toe tumor in botryomycosis, supporting the disease attribution and atypical presentation.

panels.figure_caption: On the right great toe finger exophytic, ulcerated tumor.
in_text_mentions: A 42-year-old male patient, a farmer, arrives at the dermatology service with a slow-growing lesion that had appeared 2-years earlier in the great toe finger of the right foot. The patient reported pain of moderate intensity that was enhanced with daily walking, as well as self-limited bleeding. Physical exam reveals in the dorsal aspect of the great toe finger an exophytic ulcerated tumor, erythematous, with hematic crust on the surface and some areas of bleeding, measuring 5×5 centimeters (Fig. 1).Figure 1On the right great toe finger exophytic, ulcerated tumor.Figure 1
